answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with quadratic staking anchored at a trusted wharf: each agent locks a bond into the kernel, but voting weight rises only as the square root of that bond. Splitting one stake across a thousand fake personas therefore buys the same influence for a thousand times the cost. To earn K votes an attacker must post K squared in locked collateral, while honest agents hold one credential each. Inventing a fable of many identities stops paying, because the bill grows faster than the power it buys.
